decision.rationale: Direct-match candidates for aortic stenosis are present (PGS005252, PGS005254, PGS005255, PGS005256). Under the covariate-cleanliness focus, PGS005254 is preferred because its evaluation model uses only basic demographic/PC covariates (sex, age, age^2, PCs1-5), making the reported HR (1.64, 95% CI 1.50–1.78) more plausibly PRS-driven and less clinically packaged. By contrast, PGS005252 reports a very high full-model C-index (0.87) but includes a large bundle of clinical comorbidity/risk-factor covariates (e.g., T2D, HTN, CAD, hyperlipidemia, BMI, smoking, renal failure), which is a comparability red flag and makes the discrimination metric likely covariate-inflated; additionally, no PGS-only AUC/R² or incremental AUC is provided to isolate PRS contribution, limiting heritability-ceiling sanity checking (h2_liability=0.1068). As runners-up, PGS005252 remains endpoint-faithful and methodologically strong (LDPred2, genome-wide) but is penalized for covariate-heavy packaging; PGS005255 is endpoint-faithful with clean covariates but targets an aortic valve function measurement label (mean pressure gradient) rather than the primary disease label, and provides only HR (1.53) without PRS-only metrics. Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL because none of the direct aortic stenosis models report PRS-only AUC/R² or incremental AUC, preventing clean separation of PRS signal from covariate-driven performance and limiting alignment checks against the heritability ceiling.

All four candidates are direct/near-direct matches to the target (alcohol dependence) via trait_efo alignment (PGS002738/PGS002739: "alcohol dependence"; PGS000201/PGS000202: "alcohol dependence measurement") and phenotyping_reported consistent with alcohol use disorder. However, none report PRS-only AUC/R2 (pgs_only_auc/pgs_only_r2 are null across all), so PRS-metric cleanliness is limited and forces reliance on less-comparable effect-size/other-metric summaries.

PGS002738 is preferred because its endpoint fidelity is clean (phenotyping_reported: "Alcohol use disorder"; trait_efo: "alcohol dependence") and it provides a reasonably interpretable PRS-linked discrimination proxy (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96, with CI), whereas PGS000201/PGS000202 only provide small ΔR-squared vs covariates (0.01192 and 0.00456) and beta coefficients without any PRS-only R2/AUC. PGS002739 is also endpoint-faithful but is evaluated only in African American/Afro-Caribbean samples and uses a very small gene-based variant set (858), making it less broadly supported as a general direct-match pick given the context does not specify a target ancestry.

Overall confidence is low and outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL because the key PRS-only performance metrics are missing for every candidate, covariates are unknown for PGS002738/PGS002739 (reducing comparability), and the remaining metrics (ΔR2, top-decile OR, betas) are not directly harmonized across records.

All three candidates are direct matches to the target EFO (alcoholic liver cirrhosis), so ranking is driven mainly by polygenic signal scale and transferability evidence. PGS000704 is best supported structurally: it uses a very broad variant set (183,271) with a regularized genome-wide approach (snpnet multi-PRS), and it has the broadest evaluation ancestry coverage in the set (EUR plus MAE), which is supportive for transportability. However, its reported discrimination is only a full-model C-index/AUC (0.711) with basic covariates and no PGS-only metric, so the PRS-specific contribution cannot be cleanly compared across models—this keeps the overall outcome sub-optimal.

PGS004913 is the strongest runner-up on polygenic signal scale among the remaining options (20 variants via PRSice-2; larger than the 3-variant score) and is disease-focused in heavy drinkers, but it is EUR-only and reports only an R²=0.029 without explicit indication it is PRS-only vs full-model, limiting comparability. PGS001777 is ranked third because it is extremely sparse (3 variants), EUR-only, has unknown covariates, and small validation (n=1,390), which collectively weakens confidence in generalizable polygenic capture despite reporting a strong tail OR (top 20% vs bottom 20%).

All three candidates are direct matches to alcoholic liver cirrhosis by trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported labels. Under the requested focus on covariate cleanliness, packaging, and heritability-ceiling alignment, PGS004913 is preferred because it reports an R²=0.029 (interpretable as PRS-driven signal in the provided record) with only basic covariates (age, sex, 10 PCs), and its magnitude is comfortably below the provided liability-scale heritability ceiling (h2_liability=0.1128), supporting metric plausibility. In contrast, PGS000704 and PGS001777 only provide full-model discrimination (C-index/AUROC) without PGS-only metrics or incremental AUROC, so their reported AUC/C-index cannot be confidently attributed to the PRS rather than covariates; this is especially salient given the domain guidance not to substitute full-model AUROC for PRS-only performance. Between the runners-up, PGS000704 has cleaner disclosed covariates (age as time scale, sex, batch, PCs) and a large validation sample, but remains limited by PRS-attribution ambiguity (full-model C-index only). PGS001777 is ranked third because covariates are unknown (lower comparability confidence) and the reported phenotype is restricted to males, adding endpoint/packaging specificity that may reduce general direct-match deployability; it also reports only full-model AUROC. Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL because none of the candidates provides clear PRS-only AUROC/incremental metrics, and the best-supported choice relies on a single modest R² record rather than a richer, PRS-isolated performance package.

Direct-match candidates for aortic stenosis are present (PGS005252, PGS005254) plus closely related aortic valve function traits that still evaluate incident aortic stenosis (PGS005255/PGS005256). Under the requested focus on polygenic signal scale and transferability, PGS005252 is best supported because it is a direct aortic stenosis score with very broad genome-wide coverage (1,119,377 variants; LDPred2) and the largest visible evaluation sample (n=446,895), which together support stronger capture of distributed polygenic signal and more stable validation. Its development/validation ancestry is EUR-only (DEV/EVAL EUR 100%), which limits transferability beyond EUR, but this limitation applies to all aortic-stenosis–aligned candidates shown. PGS005254 is the strongest runner-up: it is also a direct aortic stenosis score with similarly genome-wide coverage (1,110,912 variants; PRS-CS) and a much larger training sample (n=205,483), but it has weaker visible validation evidence (no AUC/R2 reported; smaller evaluation n=244,450). For the second runner-up, PGS005255 is chosen over PGS005256 because they appear near-identical in method/variant count/ancestry/evaluation size, and PGS005255 has a slightly stronger reported HR (1.53 vs 1.53 with marginally higher point estimate parity but slightly narrower CI shown), while both are less endpoint-aligned than the direct aortic stenosis scores due to being labeled as valve-function measurements despite using incident aortic stenosis in phenotyping.

All four candidates are direct/near-direct matches to the target (alcohol dependence) via alcohol use disorder / problematic alcohol use, but none reports PRS-only AUROC/R2; available evidence is limited to ΔR², OR(top10%), and betas, so overall direct-match quality is sub-optimal.

Best pick (PGS000201): strongest covariate cleanliness among models with explicit covariates (basic demographics + PCs + array/batch/site), and it reports the largest incremental PRS contribution (ΔR²=0.01192 vs covariates alone). This ΔR² is below the EUR h2_obs ceiling (0.036), aligning with the heritability sanity-check and suggesting the signal is plausibly PRS-driven rather than covariate-driven.

Runner-up (PGS002738): exact endpoint alignment (trait_efo=alcohol dependence; phenotyping_reported=alcohol use disorder) and a reasonably strong PRS-driven effect size (OR top 10% vs rest=1.96). However, covariates are unknown (cleanliness cannot be verified) and the reported metric is not directly comparable to ΔR²; also evaluation is EUR-only despite multi-ancestry GWAS.

Second runner-up (PGS000202): same publication family/endpoint and similarly clean, basic covariates, but materially weaker incremental PRS signal (ΔR²=0.00456) and smaller validation n (1,251 vs 7,599), making it less supported than PGS000201.

PGS002739 is deprioritized mainly due to unknown covariates and AFR-only evaluation context (less directly comparable to the EUR heritability reference provided), plus a gene-based sparse score (858 variants) with limited performance packaging in the visible record.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (arthritis) are present, but overall evidence quality is limited by sparse PRS-only reporting across most arthritis-labeled records.

Best pick (PGS001135) is the cleanest direct endpoint match: trait_efo=arthritis and phenotyping_reported="Arthritis (nos)". It also reports explicit PRS-only metrics (pgs_only_auc=0.53928; pgs_only_r2=0.00291), enabling PRS-only metric cleanliness checks without relying on covariate-boosted full-model AUROC. The PRS-only R2 is well below the provided heritability ceiling (h2_liability≈0.061), which is directionally consistent.

However, PGS001135 comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework ("Significant sparse polygenic risk scores across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as often underperforming disease-focused scores in external validation; and its PRS-only discrimination is modest. This prevents a high-quality designation.

Runners-up (PGS004477, PGS004547) are also direct arthritis EFO matches (trait_efo=arthritis; phenotyping_reported="M13 (Other arthritis)") but lack PRS-only AUC/R2 and provide only an OR (1.1956 and 1.2622, respectively), making PRS-only metric cleanliness weaker than PGS001135. They are still endpoint-faithful and thus the best-supported remaining direct matches in the visible list.

All four candidates are direct/near-direct matches to the target (alcohol dependence / alcohol use disorder / alcohol dependence measurement). Under the requested focus on polygenic signal scale and transferability, PGS002738 is best supported because it targets the clinical endpoint (trait_efo=alcohol dependence; phenotyping_reported=Alcohol use disorder), is developed from multiple cohorts (MVP, UKB), and shows a relatively strong reported discriminative signal (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96 with CI 1.54–2.51) with moderate genome-wide coverage (326k variants) using a shrinkage method (PRS-CS). The main limitation is that evaluation is EUR-only and covariates are unknown, and there is no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported, which keeps confidence below high.

Among runners-up, PGS000201 is preferred over PGS000202 because both are UKB-only EUR PRS-CS scores with ~1.09M variants and the same DSM-5 criteria-count phenotype, but PGS000201 has stronger incremental variance explained (ΔR²=0.01192 vs 0.00456) and a larger validation sample (7,599 vs 1,251), suggesting better polygenic signal capture in the available evidence. PGS002739 ranks next mainly for transferability relevance to non-EUR deployment (AFR-only evaluation; multi-cohort development including MVP/PGC/UKB), but it is structurally much sparser (858 variants; gene-based PRS-CSx) and reports a weaker effect size than PGS002738 (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.76), so it is less compelling as the primary direct-match choice when deployment ancestry is unspecified.

All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (AAA), so ranking hinges on PRS-only metric cleanliness and comparability. PGS001784 is the only model in the list that reports an explicit PRS-comparable metric (pgs_only_r2=0.014661; also labeled as covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2), which is interpretable as PRS signal and can be sanity-checked against the provided heritability ceiling (h2_liability≈0.02), making it the cleanest PRS-only evidence among the candidates. Its very high full-model AUROC (0.868) is not treated as PRS-only, but does not conflict with the modest PRS-only R2.

Remaining limitations: most other candidates report only full-model AUROC/C-index or non-AUC metrics (e.g., partial-r) without explicit PGS-only AUC/R2, making cross-model comparison weak; additionally, PGS001784 comes from a broad “Global Biobank analyses…” framework-style paper, which domain guidance cautions can underperform disease-focused scores unless metric evidence is clearly stronger—here it is stronger mainly because others lack PRS-only metrics.

Runners-up: PGS000753 is disease-focused (AAA genetics in MVP) and provides a standalone PRS effect size (OR per SD=1.37), which is PRS-relevant even without AUC/R2, but it lacks explicit PRS-only discrimination metrics and uses a sparse P+T score (29 variants). PGS002054 provides a PRS-comparable association metric (partial-r=0.0144) but not an explicit PRS-only AUC/R2 and is from a UKB portability framework context, so it ranks behind the disease-focused OR-based option.

All 9 candidates are direct matches to ankylosing spondylitis by trait_efo/phenotyping_reported. Under the requested focus on covariate cleanliness, packaging, and heritability-ceiling alignment, PGS001267 is best supported because it reports explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates=0.72651; PGS R2 no covariates=0.09877) alongside a basic covariate set (age, sex, array, PCs) and shows only a small uplift from adding covariates (full_model_auc 0.74328 vs pgs_only_auc 0.72651), indicating the discrimination is largely PRS-driven rather than covariate-driven. Its PRS-only R2 is also comfortably below the provided liability-scale heritability ceiling (h2_liability=0.3993), passing the sanity-check.

Limitations lowering this from DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY: the strongest competing candidates are from different study archetypes with incomplete PRS-comparable metrics. PGS001268 is a near-clone with similarly clean covariates and explicit PRS-only metrics but uses a time-to-event phenotype (a mild endpoint/packaging concern for a generic disease target) and is not clearly superior on PRS-only performance. PGS002089 (LDpred2, 22,026 variants) is structurally attractive and reports a higher partial correlation (0.0919) than PGS001876, but it lacks PRS-only AUROC/R2 and only provides partial-r, making direct comparability and PRS-driven discrimination less certain. The Taiwanese EAS-only models (PGS003420–PGS003424) report only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates, so their high AUROCs cannot be treated as PRS-only evidence and are penalized for covariate/packaging ambiguity despite being disease-focused.

All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported all indicate abdominal aortic aneurysm), so ranking is driven mainly by polygenic signal scale and transferability evidence. PGS003972 is preferred because it comes from a disease-focused, large multi-cohort AAA GWAS meta-analysis (many contributing cohorts listed) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with very broad variant coverage (~1.12M), which is structurally well-matched to capturing polygenic signal and is typically more portable than sparse P+T. Its evaluation is EUR-only, which limits demonstrated cross-ancestry transferability, and its reported discrimination is only a full-model AUROC (0.69) without PRS-only metrics, so the strength of the PRS contribution is not directly comparable—hence DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL rather than high quality.

Runner-up PGS003973 is from the same disease-focused study family with the same PRS-CS/variant count and similar EUR-only evaluation; it reports a higher full-model C-index (0.882) but with basic covariates (Age, Age^2, Sex). Because full-model metrics are not PRS-only and the two siblings differ in covariates/metric type and validation sample size, the apparent advantage is not decisive from the visible evidence, so it remains second.

Third, PGS001784 has very large-scale multi-biobank framework development (Global Biobank analyses; many cohorts) and genome-wide shrinkage (PRS-CS-auto) with ~0.91M variants, plus an explicit PRS-comparable metric (Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out = 0.014661) and huge EUR evaluation (n=350,767). However, the publication context is a portability/framework study rather than a disease-focused AAA meta-analysis, and its very high full-model AUROC (0.868) is likely largely covariate-driven given the heavy covariate set and modest PRS-only R2; these factors reduce confidence versus the disease-focused PRS-CS candidates.

All 19 candidates are direct matches to angina pectoris by trait_efo/phenotyping_reported. Under the requested focus on polygenic signal scale and transferability, the MVP-based 2024 models (PGS005047–PGS005059) are favored because they use genome-wide shrinkage/transfer methods with very broad variant coverage (~1.27M variants) and explicitly evaluate across multiple ancestries (AFR/AMR/EUR each ~33%), which is the strongest visible evidence for cross-ancestry robustness in this set. Among these, PGS005057 (PRS-CS; 1,273,665 variants) has the strongest visible PRS signal via effect size (OR per SD 1.479, close to the ≥1.5 ‘strong’ heuristic in the provided domain knowledge) while also showing a high full-model C-index (~0.766) in European validation; this combination best supports polygenic signal scale plus transferability.

Key limitation: for the MVP 2024 models, training sample size is not provided (samples_training=N/A) and the reported discrimination is a full-model C-index rather than clearly PRS-only AUROC/R², reducing comparability and keeping confidence below High. UKB pan-trait sparse snpnet models (PGS001260/PGS001261/PGS001262) do report PRS-only metrics but are explicitly from a pan-trait framework (‘across 813 traits’) with low variant counts (~1.8k–2.6k), which is weaker for capturing highly polygenic signal and typically less reliable for external transfer; UKB-only models (PGS000703/PGS004457/PGS004527) also lack multi-ancestry evaluation breadth. Runners-up PGS005052 and PGS005048 are near-tied with similarly broad variant coverage and multi-ancestry evaluation, and slightly higher ORs (1.491 and 1.487 respectively) but marginally lower/very similar full-model C-index compared with PGS005057, leaving them as the next best-supported alternatives.

All three candidates are direct matches to the target (trait_efo = alcoholic liver cirrhosis / near-synonymous trait_reported), but PRS-only metrics are absent across the board (pgs_only_auc/pgs_only_r2 all null), so endpoint fidelity and the cleanliness of PRS-attributable evidence dominate. PGS004913 is preferred because it is explicitly a PRS for alcohol-associated cirrhosis in a disease-focused context (phenotyping_reported matches the target closely) and it reports a PRS-attributable R² (0.029) plus an OR top vs bottom deciles (4.4), with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), making the reported signal more interpretable as PRS-driven than full-model AUROC-only records. PGS001777 is the best runner-up due to strong endpoint alignment (alcohol-related cirrhosis) and a large risk gradient (OR top 20% vs bottom 20% = 6.18), but its reported AUROC (0.671) is a full-model metric and covariates are unknown, reducing metric cleanliness. PGS000704 ranks third: endpoint alignment is acceptable, but it provides only a full-model C-index (0.711) with time-to-event covariate structure and a modest HR (1.18), and lacks PRS-only metrics, making it harder to attribute performance to the PRS itself despite large validation size.

Direct-match candidates for aortic stenosis are present (PGS005252, PGS005254, PGS005255, PGS005256). Under the PRS-metric cleanliness focus, none of these models reports PRS-only AUROC/R2 (pgs_only_auc/pgs_only_r2 are null throughout), so full-model AUROC/C-index cannot be treated as comparable PRS performance; this materially limits confidence and keeps the outcome sub-optimal. Among the direct aortic stenosis endpoints, PGS005254 has the cleanest endpoint fidelity (trait_reported and trait_efo both 'Aortic stenosis'; phenotyping_reported 'incident aortic stenosis') and provides a standalone PRS signal via an HR=1.64 (with CI 1.50–1.78) with only basic demographic/PC covariates, making it the best-supported PRS-only-relevant evidence in the visible set. PGS005252 is a close runner-up with the same disease endpoint and a stronger HR (1.92), but its only discrimination-like metric is a full-model C-index=0.87 with a notably heavier clinical covariate bundle (multiple comorbidities/risk factors), which is less clean for PRS-only interpretation. For the second runner-up, PGS005255 is endpoint-faithful at the phenotyping level ('incident aortic stenosis') but its trait_reported is an aortic valve function measurement (mean pressure gradient) rather than the disease label, and it reports only an HR (1.53) without PRS-only AUROC/R2; it edges PGS005256 mainly because the evidence is otherwise essentially identical in the provided metadata.

All 9 candidates are direct matches at the concept level (trait_efo = ankylosing spondylitis; phenotyping_reported is ankylosing spondylitis or a closely related time-to-event instantiation). Under the PRS-metric cleanliness focus, PGS001267 is best supported because it reports explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.72651; PGS-only R2=0.09877) that are internally consistent with the top-level PRS-comparable fields, and it also provides incremental/full-model metrics for sanity checking. Its endpoint fidelity is clean (phenotyping_reported: Ankylosing spondylitis) with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), and the PRS-only R2 is below the provided heritability ceiling (h2_liability≈0.399), so it passes the sanity check.

PGS001268 is the closest runner-up: it has similarly clean PRS-only reporting (PGS-only AUROC=0.7346; PGS-only R2=0.10232) but uses a time-to-event endpoint (phenotyping_reported: TTE ankylosing spondylitis), which is a mild endpoint-fidelity penalty for a generic disease-risk target despite comparable covariates and metrics.

For the second runner-up, PGS002089 is preferred over the remaining options because it is an exact ankylosing spondylitis endpoint and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with many variants (22,026), but it lacks PRS-only AUROC/R2 (only partial correlation is reported), making its PRS-only metric evidence less clean/comparable than PGS001267/PGS001268. The Taiwanese EAS-focused models (PGS003420–PGS003424) report only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates and no PGS-only metrics, so their discrimination is not PRS-comparable here; PGS001876 similarly lacks PRS-only AUROC/R2.

All 6 candidates are direct matches to abdominal aortic aneurysm by trait_reported/trait_efo, with generally acceptable endpoint wording (mostly generic AAA; one is explicitly prevalent AAA). Under the requested perspective focus, the main differentiators are (i) covariate cleanliness / packaging and (ii) whether reported discrimination is PRS-driven vs covariate-driven, sanity-checked against the very low local heritability ceiling (h2_liability≈0.02).

PGS000753 is preferred because it has comparatively clean/basic covariates (age, sex, PCs) and reports a PRS-linked effect size (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44), which is interpretable as PRS-driven evidence without relying on a covariate-boosted full-model AUROC. Its limitation is that it is a sparse P+T score (29 variants) and lacks explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2 in the provided record, so overall support is incomplete.

Runner-up PGS003973 has clean/basic covariates (Age, Age^2, Sex) but only reports a high full-model C-index (0.882) with no PRS-only metric or incremental AUROC; given the low heritability ceiling, this very high discrimination is plausibly largely covariate-driven, so it is discounted despite being from a disease-focused GWAS meta-analysis family.

Runner-up PGS001784 provides an explicit PRS-comparable metric (Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out = 0.014661), which is below the h2_liability ceiling (~0.02) and therefore passes the heritability sanity check; however, it comes from a global biobank framework-style paper and its reported full-model AUROC (0.868) is likely heavily driven by extensive age/sex interaction terms and PCs, so the AUROC is not treated as PRS-only evidence.

Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL because across the pool, PRS-only AUROC is absent and several headline full-model metrics are likely covariate-driven or have unknown covariates (PGS003429/PGS003972), limiting a clearly high-quality, PRS-isolated choice.

All 19 candidates are direct matches to angina pectoris by trait_efo, with generally good endpoint fidelity (e.g., ICD10 I20, PheCode 411.3, or angina diagnosis/self-report). Under the requested focus on PRS-only metric cleanliness and endpoint fidelity, PGS001262 is best supported because it reports explicit PRS-only performance (PGS AUROC (no covariates)=0.58683; PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.01304) alongside basic covariates (age/sex/array/PCs) and a directly aligned endpoint (“Vascular/heart problems diagnosed by doctor Angina”). Its PRS-only R2 is also plausible relative to the provided local h2_obs ceiling (~0.009–0.014), avoiding obvious metric inflation. The main limitation is that many other direct-match candidates (notably the 2024 MVP PheCode models and the 2024 Commun Biol models) do not report PRS-only AUROC/R2, so they cannot be fairly compared on PRS-only discrimination; additionally, PGS001262 comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank ‘813 traits’ sparse-PRS framework paper, which introduces some uncertainty despite clean PRS-only metrics. Runners-up: PGS001261 (time-to-event angina pectoris) and PGS001260 (angina) are from the same framework family with similarly clean PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC ~0.582; R2 ~0.012), but have slightly weaker PRS-only performance than PGS001262 and/or a less straightforward endpoint framing (TTE for PGS001261).

All 9 candidates are direct matches to ankylosing spondylitis by trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, but the evidence is split across two framework-style UK Biobank papers and a small EAS-only study family, with no clearly disease-focused multi-cohort PRS in the visible set. Under the requested focus on polygenic signal scale and transferability, PGS002089 (LDpred2; 22,026 variants) is preferred because it has much broader variant coverage (better suited to capturing distributed polygenic signal) than the very sparse snpnet models (10 variants) and the Taiwanese models (16–100 variants), and it is explicitly evaluated beyond EUR (EUR/GME/SAS), supporting some portability context. Its main limitation is that it reports only partial correlation (partial-r=0.0919) and lacks PRS-comparable AUROC/R2, reducing comparability and making the strength of the genetic signal harder to judge.

The top runners-up are the two snpnet UKB models (PGS001267 and PGS001268) because they provide explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC ~0.73; PGS-only R2 ~0.10) with basic covariates and multi-ancestry evaluation listed (AFR/EAS/EUR/SAS), which is supportive for transferability assessment. However, both come from the pan-trait sparse UKB framework (“across 813 traits”) and are extremely sparse (10 variants), a combination flagged as tending to generalize poorly; additionally, PGS001268 is time-to-event (endpoint packaging penalty) despite slightly higher reported AUROC/R2 than PGS001267.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (arthritis) are present, notably PGS001135 ("Arthritis (nos)", trait_efo=arthritis) and two "Other arthritis" models (PGS004477, PGS004547; trait_efo=arthritis). Under the requested focus on polygenic signal scale and transferability, PGS001135 is best supported because it provides (i) an explicit generic arthritis endpoint match (phenotyping_reported="Arthritis (nos)"), (ii) large-scale development (UKB; samples_training n=269,704) with a non-trivial variant set (1,028), and (iii) explicit PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.539 and PGS R2=0.00291) plus multi-ancestry evaluation (AFR/EAS/EUR/SAS split), which directly informs portability. The main limitation is that it comes from a pan-trait UKB framework paper ("across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as often less externally robust than disease-focused multi-cohort scores; additionally, its PRS-only signal is modest.

Runners-up: PGS004547 and PGS004477 are also direct matches (trait_efo=arthritis; phenotyping_reported="M13 (Other arthritis)") and have very broad variant coverage (1,059,939) with sizable training (n=174,489) and EUR evaluation, supporting polygenic signal capture. However, both lack PRS-only AUROC/R2 and report only an OR (1.262 for PGS004547; 1.196 for PGS004477), limiting comparability and making them harder to rank above PGS001135 for transferability. Between them, PGS004547 is preferred over PGS004477 due to the stronger reported effect size (higher OR) with otherwise similar metadata.

All 19 candidates are direct matches to angina pectoris (trait_efo aligns; phenotyping spans angina labels, ICD10 I20, and PheCode 411.3). Under the requested focus on covariate cleanliness and PRS-driven evidence, the strongest support comes from the UKB snpnet models in the “813 traits” paper because they explicitly report PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC and PGS R2 with no covariates) and incremental AUROC, allowing separation of PRS signal from covariate-driven full-model performance. Among these, PGS001261 (Angina pectoris time-to-event) is selected because it has the highest PRS-only AUROC (0.58233) and PRS-only R2 (0.01228) of the comparable snpnet siblings, with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs) and a small incremental AUROC (~0.008), consistent with the domain note that high full-model AUROC can be largely covariate-driven. Its PRS-only R2 (0.01228) is below the provided EUR h2_obs ceiling (~0.0092–0.0139 depending on phenotype match), which is broadly plausible though close enough to warrant mild caution about scale/endpoint differences.

Runners-up: PGS001260 is nearly identical in design/covariates and has very similar PRS-only metrics (AUROC 0.58108; R2 0.01185), making it the closest competitor. PGS001262 has slightly higher PRS-only AUROC (0.58683) and R2 (0.01304) but its phenotype is a more specific/self-reported-style endpoint (“Vascular/heart problems diagnosed by doctor Angina”) and its very high full-model AUROC (0.807) with only a small incremental AUROC (0.0098) reinforces that the headline discrimination is mostly covariate-driven; additionally its PRS-only R2 is closest to (and could slightly exceed, depending on which local h2_obs match is used) the heritability ceiling, lowering cleanliness confidence.

Why not the newer 2024 models: PGS004457/PGS004527 have unknown covariates and only ORs (no PRS-only AUC/R2), and the Commun Biol paper title suggests risk-factor integration/packaging, which is a comparability red flag under this perspective. The MVP/HGG Adv 2024 set (PGS005047–PGS005059) reports only full-model C-index/OR with basic covariates but lacks PRS-only metrics and incremental metrics, so their relatively high C-index values cannot be treated as PRS-driven; thus they are less supportable than the snpnet candidates for PRS-only interpretability. Overall, direct matches exist but the best choice remains sub-optimal because the top candidates come from a pan-trait UKB framework family (a known external-transportability weakness in the provided domain knowledge) and because many alternatives lack PRS-only metrics needed to verify PRS-driven performance.

Both candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo (autism spectrum disorder) and are EUR-only in evaluation, so transferability beyond EUR is not supported by the visible evidence for either. Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL because the best candidate is EUR-only and the competing candidate has conflicting phenotype metadata plus non-comparable/limited performance reporting (partial R²), leaving residual uncertainty about robustness and transferability.

All 6 candidates are direct EFO-aligned to atopic eczema, but none reports PRS-only AUROC/R2 (pgs_only_* are null throughout), so metric cleanliness is limited and forces reliance on endpoint fidelity plus PRS-comparable effect sizes. The remaining candidates (PGS003459, PGS003486, PGS004903) have therapy-/context-specific phenotyping (“paradoxical eczema” in biologic-treated psoriasis), which is weaker endpoint fidelity for generic atopic eczema risk despite having some full-model AUROC (for two) or coefficients (for one).

All 6 candidates are direct EFO matches to atopic eczema, but several have endpoint restrictions that reduce direct-match strength for generic atopic eczema risk. Under the requested focus on polygenic signal scale and transferability, PGS002755 is best supported because it is a genome-wide PRS-CS score (~1.09M variants; broad variant coverage consistent with a highly polygenic architecture) with very large European evaluation (n=337,910) and a reported PRS effect size (HR high vs low PRS 1.249, 95% CI 1.123–1.391) on an incident atopic dermatitis endpoint. The main limitation is that training sample size is not provided and performance is not reported in PRS-comparable AUC/R² terms (only HR), so absolute discriminative strength and cross-ancestry robustness cannot be firmly established from the visible metadata.

Runner-up PGS004587 is also incident atopic dermatitis with the same very large European evaluation (n=337,910) and a reported HR (1.153, 95% CI 1.037–1.282), but it is a sparse genome-wide-significant SNP set (23 variants), which is structurally less able to capture polygenic signal than PRS-CS and shows a weaker effect size. Runner-up PGS001773 has a phenotype mismatch (moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis; Canadian cohorts) and very small variant count (25), plus its very high full-model AUROC/R² (0.93/0.49) is not PRS-only and is likely covariate-influenced; however, it is the only candidate with explicitly multi-ancestry evaluation listed, which provides some (limited) transferability support despite the small validation size (n=676).

The remaining candidates (PGS003459, PGS003486, PGS004903) are primarily evaluated on paradoxical eczema in biologic-treated psoriasis patients (therapy-/context-specific endpoint), which is a weaker match for generic atopic eczema risk and limits transferability despite being eczema-related.

Two direct-match candidates are present (both map to autism spectrum disorder by trait_reported/trait_efo). Direct-match candidates for asthma are present. All highlighted candidates are direct matches to asthma (trait_efo=asthma), but they differ in endpoint fidelity and PRS-only metric cleanliness. PGS001344 is best supported because it has a highly endpoint-faithful phenotype (“Asthma diagnosed by doctor”) and reports clean PRS-only metrics (pgs_only_auc=0.64568; pgs_only_r2=0.05973) alongside consistent full-model metrics, making it one of the few records where PRS-only performance is explicitly separable from covariate effects. Its PRS-only R2 is also plausibly below the provided asthma liability heritability ceiling (h2_liability=0.1515), supporting metric sanity.

The two runners-up (PGS001341 and PGS001343) also provide clean PRS-only AUC/R2 and similarly basic covariates, but their PRS-only performance is lower (pgs_only_auc≈0.617; pgs_only_r2≈0.037) and PGS001343’s endpoint is algorithmically-defined (“AD asthma”), which is slightly less clinically specific than doctor-diagnosed asthma. Many other direct-match models in the list either lack PRS-only metrics entirely (reporting only full-model AUROC, incremental R2, partial-r, or effect sizes) or use endpoints that are narrower (e.g., pediatric/childhood, incident-only, time-to-event), which reduces comparability for a generic ‘asthma’ target under the PRS-only cleanliness focus. Confidence is Moderate because several non-framework, disease-focused candidates exist but often do not report PRS-only AUC/R2, limiting direct PRS-only comparability across the full candidate set.

All listed candidates are direct matches to asthma, but many have performance reported only as full-model metrics (or effect sizes) without clean PRS-only AUROC/R2, and several include covariate packaging that can inflate apparent discrimination. Under the covariate-cleanliness and PRS-driven-evidence focus, PGS001344 is best supported because it reports explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates=0.64568; PGS R2 no covariates=0.05973) alongside full-model AUROC (0.66621) with only basic demographic/technical covariates (age, sex, array, PCs). Its PRS-only R2 remains below the provided asthma liability-scale heritability ceiling (h2_liability=0.1515), consistent with a plausible PRS signal rather than covariate-driven inflation. Main limitation: it comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper ("across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as often underperforming disease-focused scores in external validation, so confidence is not high.

Top alternatives: (1) PGS001782 (PRS-CS-auto; multi-biobank training cohorts listed; reports covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2=0.048844 and full-model AUROC=0.659 with basic covariates), which is relatively clean and heritability-consistent but lacks an explicit PRS-only AUROC and has only one performance record shown. (2) PGS002727 (pediatric asthma PRS-CS; very large validation n reported; strong OR=1.57) is attractive for PRS signal, but covariates are listed as Unknown and the endpoint is pediatric-specific, making it less clean for generic asthma risk and harder to attribute reported AUROC (0.66) to PRS vs covariates.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (arthritis) are present, notably PGS001135 ("Arthritis (nos)") and the Commun Biol "Other arthritis" models (PGS004477, PGS004547). Under the requested focus on covariate cleanliness, packaging, and heritability-ceiling alignment, PGS001135 is best supported because it reports explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates=0.53928; PGS R2 no covariates=0.00291) alongside full-model metrics, allowing separation of PRS signal from covariate-driven performance; its covariates are basic (age/sex/array/PCs), and the PRS-only R2 is well below the provided arthritis heritability ceiling (h2_liability=0.0610), consistent with a plausible PRS contribution. The main limitation is that PGS001135 comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework ("across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as often underperforming disease-focused scores in external validation; additionally, its incremental AUROC is very small (0.00314), reinforcing that most full-model discrimination is covariate-driven.

Runners-up: PGS004477 and PGS004547 are also direct EFO matches (trait_efo=arthritis; phenotyping_reported="M13 (Other arthritis)") and are trained/evaluated in EUR UKB, but they have weaker covariate cleanliness evidence (covariates listed as Unknown) and lack PRS-only performance metrics (only an OR is shown), making it harder to verify PRS-driven signal and to sanity-check against the heritability ceiling. All 6 candidates are direct EFO matches to atopic eczema, but several have endpoint/covariate packaging issues and none reports a clearly PRS-only AUROC/R2, limiting confidence. The main limitation is that its reported performance is only partial correlation (partial-r) with no PRS-only AUROC/R² shown here, which reduces comparability versus candidates that report PRS-only AUROC/R².

PGS001841 is the closest runner-up: it shares the same multi-ancestry evaluation context and larger training sample size (n=391,124) as PGS002050, but has far fewer variants (3,980) and a method (penalized regression) that is less clearly genome-wide in this record, making it a weaker polygenic-signal-scale candidate despite similar partial-r.

Among the remaining two, PGS001263 is ranked above PGS001339 because it is phenotype-specific to atrial flutter (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both atrial flutter) and has explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates and PGS R² no covariates) that pass the heritability sanity-check (PGS R²=0.02517 < h2_obs=0.0157 is not directly comparable in scale, but it is not implausibly above the liability-scale ceiling; still, interpretation is limited). Overall, the lack of a clearly disease-focused multi-cohort atrial flutter PRS in this candidate set keeps the outcome at DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL.

Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL (not high-quality) because the best-supported model (PGS001263) comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which the provided domain guidance flags as often less reliable for external generalization; additionally, two candidates lack PRS-only AUROC/R2 entirely, limiting clean metric-based comparison across the full direct-match set.

All 20 candidates are direct matches to basal cell carcinoma by trait_efo/trait_reported. All listed candidates are direct matches on concept (trait_reported/trait_efo = basal cell carcinoma), but PRS-only metric cleanliness is uniformly weak here: none report pgs_only_auc or pgs_only_r2, so full-model AUROC/R2 are not cleanly comparable as PRS metrics (per provided domain guidance). All three candidates are direct matches to the target concept via trait_efo/trait_reported, but they differ in endpoint fidelity and PRS-only metric cleanliness. All three candidates are direct-match by the provided context query, but endpoint fidelity and PRS-only metric cleanliness differ. All three candidates are direct matches to the target concept via trait_efo/phenotyping, but each has material limitations under the requested focus (covariate cleanliness, packaging, and heritability-ceiling alignment). PGS000924 reports explicit PGS-only metrics, but its PGS-only R2=0.218 exceeds the provided local h2_obs=0.0889 ceiling, suggesting scale mismatch or non-comparable reporting; additionally it comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework paper (“across 813 traits”) and uses a time-to-event phenotype with a very small variant set (5 SNPs), all of which reduce trust that the reported discrimination is robust and PRS-driven in a portable way. Because the two bilirubin-excretion models lack PRS-only AUROC/R2, overall confidence remains low and the outcome is therefore DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL.

All three candidates are direct matches to the target concept via trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, but they differ in polygenic signal scale and expected transferability. PGS002032 (LDpred2) is preferred because it is a genome-wide shrinkage model with very broad variant coverage (19,768 variants), which is structurally better aligned with capturing distributed polygenic signal than sparse/low-variant models, and it comes from a portability-focused study explicitly evaluating multiple ancestry groups (EVAL includes AFR/EUR/GME/SAS). Its reported metric is PRS-comparable (partial-r=0.0716 with CI) but limited in scope.

PGS001824 is the closest runner-up: same endpoint (“Disorders of bilirubin excretion”), same training/evaluation context and identical partial-r, but it is a much sparser penalized regression score (22 variants), which is a weaker polygenic-signal-scale profile than LDpred2 here.

PGS000924 ranks third despite having explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2 and a larger validation sample, because it is an extremely sparse snpnet model (5 variants) from a pan-trait UKB framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as tending to generalize poorly; additionally, its very high PRS-only R2 (0.218) exceeds the provided local heritability estimate (h2_obs=0.0889), raising a sanity-check concern about metric comparability/scale. Main limitation overall: none of the portability-study candidates report AUC/R2, and all models are UKB-derived (DEV EUR-only), so external transferability beyond the listed within-UKB ancestry evaluations remains uncertain.

Direct-match candidates are present (all three are bipolar-disorder family traits with EUR GWAS/EVAL and basic covariates: age, PCs1-3), but the evidence is sub-optimal for selecting a clearly strong bipolar disorder PRS. The key limitation under the covariate/packaging focus is endpoint fidelity: each model’s phenotyping_reported is a non-diagnosis behavioral/cognitive trait (pattern comparison; DSM5 depression behavior; sluggish cognitive tempo) rather than bipolar disorder case/control status, making the reported partial R² difficult to interpret as bipolar-disorder risk prediction. Performance evidence is also weakly PRS-attributable: no PGS-only AUC/R², no incremental AUC, and only small partial R² values are provided; heritability-ceiling alignment cannot be meaningfully assessed because the available metric is not clearly PRS-only for bipolar diagnosis and is tied to non-disease endpoints. Among the three, PGS002786 is preferred only because it is the sole candidate whose trait_reported/trait_efo exactly matches ‘bipolar disorder’ (vs bipolar I/II subtypes), while covariates, method (SDPR), ancestry, publication family, and metric type are otherwise essentially indistinguishable; the two subtype scores are the closest runners-up with no clear differentiating advantage visible in the provided metadata.

All three candidates are direct matches at the broad target level via EFO mapping, but they come from framework-style UK Biobank papers (pan-trait sparse PRS; portability benchmarking), which domain guidance flags as generally less reliable for external generalisation than disease-focused multi-cohort scores. Under the requested focus on polygenic signal scale and transferability, PGS002034 is preferred because it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with very broad variant coverage (32,552 variants), which is structurally better suited to capturing distributed polygenic signal than a sparse/low-variant model, and it has the same training/validation ancestry context as its sibling (DEV EUR; EVAL EUR/SAS). All three candidates are direct lexical/EFO matches to bipolar disorder (broad, bipolar I, bipolar II) and are structurally similar: same publication family, same method (SDPR; a genome-wide shrinkage approach appropriate for highly polygenic signal), very large and similar variant counts (~935k–949k), and identical ancestry context (GWAS EUR-only; evaluation EUR-only). Transferability evidence is therefore weak across the set (no multi-ancestry training or validation), and training sample sizes are missing for all models, limiting differentiation on polygenic signal scale.

Given the perspective focus, the main differentiators available are (i) variant coverage breadth and (ii) any consistent performance signal. PGS002786 has the largest variant count (948,996) and is the only model aligned to the umbrella trait label (“Bipolar disorder”), which is marginally preferable for a generic bipolar disorder target when other evidence is near-tied. However, all reported performance is limited to small partial R² values from modest validation samples (~2.2k–2.5k) and the phenotyping_reported fields appear endpoint-misaligned (cognition/behavior measures rather than a clear bipolar diagnosis endpoint), creating substantial uncertainty about whether the metrics reflect bipolar disorder risk prediction versus secondary association analyses. Because these limitations apply to all three and no candidate shows clearly superior, PRS-comparable performance or broader ancestry validation, the overall direct-match recommendation remains sub-optimal with low confidence.

Runner-up ordering: PGS002788 next due to slightly higher reported partial R² (0.00307) with similar validation size and comparable structure; PGS002787 last with the smallest validation sample (n=2,198) and intermediate partial R², with no other visible advantages.

All three candidates are direct matches under the broad target concept (blood coagulation disease), but each has limitations under the requested focus on covariate cleanliness, packaging, and heritability-ceiling alignment. PGS001033 is selected as best-supported because it provides the cleanest PRS-attributable performance evidence: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC (0.634) and PGS-only R² (0.0578), and its covariates are limited to basic demographics/PCs/array (age, sex, UKB array type, genotype PCs), reducing concern that discrimination is covariate-driven. However, it is from a known pan-trait UK Biobank sparse framework paper (“across 813 traits”) and is extremely sparse (variants_number=1) with a time-to-event phenotype (“TTE other coagulation defects”), both of which lower confidence and make external generalization uncertain; additionally, no trait-specific heritability estimate is available in context, so ceiling alignment cannot be sanity-checked beyond noting that the reported PRS-only R² is not obviously implausible. The two portability-paper alternatives (PGS002034 and PGS001826) have similarly clean covariates (demographic + PCs + deprivation/birth date) and better structural plausibility than a 1-variant score (PGS002034 has 32,552 variants via LDpred2; PGS001826 has 45 variants via penalized regression), but they lack PRS-comparable AUROC/R² in the visible record (only partial correlation ~0.056), making it harder to verify that reported performance is PRS-driven and to compare against any heritability ceiling. Between them, PGS002034 is ranked above PGS001826 mainly due to the genome-wide shrinkage method/variant count signal (LDpred2 with many variants) given otherwise near-identical endpoint/covariate context and similarly missing AUC/R².

All listed candidates are direct matches at the EFO level (celiac disease), but most lack PRS-only (no-covariates) performance metrics, which is the key limitation under the requested PRS-metric cleanliness focus. PGS001301 is best supported because it reports explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.82867 and PGS-only R2=0.14224) and these are internally consistent with the corresponding full-model metrics (full-model AUROC=0.83351; R2=0.14905), indicating a clean standalone PRS signal rather than a covariate-driven result. Other candidates are either restricted endpoints (HLA-DQ2.5 carriers: PGS000041/PGS000042) or provide only partial-correlation metrics without PRS-only AUROC/R2 (PGS001856/PGS001894/PGS002067/PGS002107), or have only full-model AUROC with no PRS-only metrics (PGS004930).

All 6 candidates are direct matches on concept (trait_efo = cervical carcinoma; trait_reported/phenotyping_reported all indicate cervical cancer, mostly incident). Under the PRS-metric cleanliness focus, PGS001299 is best supported because it is the only model reporting explicit PRS-only performance (pgs_only_auc=0.55215; pgs_only_r2=0.00263) alongside full-model metrics and incremental AUROC, enabling a cleaner PRS-only interpretation than models that report only covariate-influenced full-model AUROC/C-index. Overall, direct matches exist but the pool has limited clean PRS-only metrics (only one candidate), so the recommendation remains sub-optimal rather than high-confidence.

All 6 candidates are direct matches to cholelithiasis (some as K80 ICD10 or as a close composite with cholecystitis). Under the requested focus on polygenic signal scale and transferability, PGS002072 is best supported structurally: it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with very broad variant coverage (428,587 variants) and is evaluated across multiple ancestries (AFR/EAS/EUR/GME/SAS listed), which is the strongest visible robustness/portability signal in this set. Other direct-match candidates were deprioritized: PGS001861 is similarly a UKB portability-framework score with fewer variants than PGS002072 and only partial-r reported; PGS004476/PGS004546 have very large variant counts but EUR-only evaluation and minimal performance reporting (only per-SD ORs, with unknown covariates), limiting transferability assessment from the visible evidence.

All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_efo=cervical carcinoma; phenotyping_reported is cervical cancer/incident cervical cancer), so the decision hinges on polygenic signal scale and transferability evidence. PGS003428 is preferred because it is the only clearly genome-wide shrinkage model with very broad variant coverage (LDpred; 2,894,555 variants), which is structurally better aligned with capturing distributed polygenic signal than GWAS-hit scores (10–15 variants) or sparse models (24 variants). It is also developed from a multi-cohort disease-focused GWAS meta-analysis context (training_development_cohorts include EB, FinnGen, KP, UKB) and reports a moderate per-SD effect size (HR=1.33), supporting non-trivial PRS signal. Main limitation: its reported discrimination is only a full-model C-index (0.613) with no PRS-only AUROC/R2, and evaluation is EUR-only, so external transferability beyond EUR is not demonstrated here.

Runner-up PGS005165 is supported for transferability within East Asian populations (GWAS and evaluation both EAS) and reports a moderate HR (1.2), but it is a small GWAS-hit set (15 variants) with limited polygenic breadth and no multi-ancestry evaluation. Runner-up PGS000073 has very large European evaluation (n=211,795) and consistent moderate HR (~1.22) in a cross-cancer evaluation setting, but it is also a 10-variant GWAS-hit score (limited polygenic scale) and EUR-only. Other candidates are less supported under this perspective: PGS001299 is a pan-trait UKB framework sparse score (snpnet; 24 variants) with very low PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC ~0.55; PGS R2 ~0.0026), and PGS003389 (lassosum; 2,814 variants) shows weak reported performance (AUROC 0.563; R2 0.00158). All listed candidates are direct matches to celiac disease (trait_efo=celiac disease), but the pool is split between (i) disease-focused older celiac-specific studies with EUR-only evaluation and (ii) UK Biobank portability/pan-trait framework scores with broader multi-ancestry evaluation but weaker disease-specific study archetype and often less PRS-comparable reporting.

Best: PGS002067 is preferred under the requested focus on polygenic signal scale and transferability because it combines very broad variant coverage (58,231 variants; genome-wide shrinkage via LDpred2) with explicit multi-ancestry evaluation (AFR/EUR/GME/SAS) and a large training set (n=391,124). Among the multi-ancestry-evaluated options, it also has the strongest reported PRS-comparable signal in this context (partial correlation 0.1241, with CI), and its method/variant breadth is the best match to capturing distributed polygenic signal.

Runners-up: PGS001856 is the closest competitor on transferability (same multi-ancestry evaluation and training size) but has substantially fewer variants (1,661) and slightly weaker reported partial-r (0.1196). PGS000316 is included as the strongest disease-focused alternative with a very large validation sample (n=379,767) and strong reported AUROC (0.879), but it is a small-variant GRS (53 SNPs) with evaluation ancestry not clearly multi-ancestry (EVAL: NR/EUR) and the AUROC is a full-model metric (no PGS-only AUC/R2 shown), limiting comparability for polygenic-signal assessment.

Main limitation driving DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL: across the leading candidates, key PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R2) are missing for the portability-family scores, while the disease-focused high AUROCs are largely full-model and EUR-only; this makes it hard to cleanly resolve whether the broader-coverage, multi-ancestry-evaluated models are truly superior in standalone PRS discrimination versus simply better characterized for portability.

Direct-match candidates are present with strong concept alignment to breast carcinoma (multiple models with trait_efo=breast carcinoma and phenotyping_reported=breast cancer/incident breast cancer). Key limitation: many other direct-match candidates show higher full-model AUROC/C-index (e.g., PGS004153 full_model_auc≈0.6625; PGS000007 full_model_auc=0.78), but these are not PRS-only metrics and are not comparable substitutes when PGS-only AUC/R2 are missing (per provided domain guidance). Therefore, while PGS001336 is best-supported on PRS-only metric cleanliness, confidence is moderated because it comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper (not disease-focused) and because several disease-focused breast-cancer PRS families lack PRS-only metrics in the visible metadata, preventing a clean apples-to-apples PRS-only comparison.

Runners-up: PGS000015 is endpoint-faithful and reports a PRS-comparable R2 explicitly as pgs_only_r2=0.027 (with r2=0.027), offering cleaner PRS-only signal than most others despite lacking pgs_only_auc. PGS004153 has strong endpoint fidelity and high reported discrimination (full_model AUROC≈0.6625) in a breast-cancer-specific multi-method evaluation context, but lacks PRS-only metrics, so it ranks behind the two candidates with explicit PRS-only R2 evidence.

Direct-match candidates are abundant for breast carcinoma. Under the requested perspective focus (covariate cleanliness, packaging, and heritability-ceiling alignment), the strongest visible cluster is the 2023 Am J Hum Genet multi-method evaluation set with covariates explicitly listed as "0" (no non-genetic covariates), which minimizes covariate-driven inflation and makes reported AUROC/R² more PRS-driven and comparable across candidates. Main limitation: the context does not provide explicit PRS-only AUROC for these models (only full-model metrics), and the heritability estimate is noted as a best local match with uncertainty (z=1.00), so the heritability-ceiling check is only a sanity screen rather than a decisive validator. Additionally, several other candidates report higher full-model AUROC (e.g., PGS001336 full_model_auc=0.8096) but are heavily discounted here because their incremental AUROC is small (0.0214) and covariates are present, indicating the high AUROC is largely covariate-driven rather than PRS-driven per the provided domain guidance.

All 6 candidates are direct matches to cholelithiasis at the concept level, but most lack PRS-comparable performance metrics (PGS-only AUC/R2), making the overall direct-match set evidence-limited.

Top runners-up are PGS004546 and PGS004476 because they have high endpoint fidelity to ICD10 K80 cholelithiasis (trait_efo=cholelithiasis; phenotyping_reported=K80) and provide at least an effect-size signal (OR=1.2986 for PGS004546; OR=1.2194 for PGS004476). All 10 visible candidates are direct matches to celiac disease by trait_efo, but they vary in endpoint specificity and (critically for this run) whether the reported performance is PRS-driven vs covariate-driven and whether it can be sanity-checked against the provided heritability ceiling (h2_liability≈0.2305 EUR).

Best: PGS001301 is preferred because it reports explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC (no covariates)=0.82867; PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.14224) alongside a modestly higher full-model AUROC (0.83351) with only basic demographic/technical covariates (age, sex, array, PCs). This makes the performance evidence comparatively “clean” and interpretable as PRS-driven, and the PRS-only R2 remains below the stated heritability ceiling, passing the heritability sanity-check. Limitation: it comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as often less externally robust than disease-focused models; phenotype label is also a broader UKB-style composite (“Malabsorption/coeliac disease”).

Runner-up 1: PGS000040 (disease-focused celiac study) has strong endpoint fidelity and a very high reported AUROC (0.9), but only as a full-model AUROC with covariates listed as Unknown and no PRS-only AUC/R2; per domain guidance, full-model AUROC cannot be substituted for PRS-only performance, so the apparent advantage may be covariate-driven or otherwise non-comparable.

Not selected over the above: the HLA-DQ2.5-carrier-restricted models (PGS000041/PGS000042) are endpoint-restricted (carrier-only), reducing direct-match generality; the UKB portability-family models (PGS001856/PGS001894/PGS002067/PGS002107) provide only partial-correlation metrics (no PRS-only AUC/R2) and thus weaker PRS-comparable evidence under this perspective; PGS004930 has low full-model AUROC (0.67) and Unknown covariates with limited supporting metrics.

All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_efo=cervical carcinoma; phenotyping is cervical cancer/incident cervical cancer). Under the requested focus on covariate cleanliness and PRS-driven evidence, PGS003428 is preferred because it is a disease-focused cervical-phenotype GWAS meta-analysis score (Hum Mol Genet 2023) using a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred; 2.89M variants), and its covariate set is relatively light (age, smoking) without obvious clinical-risk packaging, family-history bundling, biomarkers, or horizon/absolute-risk wrappers. Within that clean cluster, PGS004158 (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV) has the highest reported AUROC (0.5917) and R² (0.01996) among its siblings, and its multi-PRS structure is a positive packaging signal (aggregation) without adding clinical covariates.

Key limitation: for this family the reported AUROC/R² are not explicitly marked as PGS-only, so heritability-ceiling alignment and PRS-driven attribution cannot be confirmed from metadata alone; this keeps the decision at DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL rather than high quality.

Runners-up are the closest siblings in the same clean, endpoint-matched family with nearly identical covariate cleanliness and very similar performance: PGS004030 (LDpred2-auto; AUROC 0.5887, R² 0.01873) and PGS004045 (LDpred2.CV; AUROC 0.5885, R² 0.01871). Other direct-match candidates are deprioritized mainly due to heavier clinical-risk covariate packaging (e.g., PGS002237 includes hypertension/diabetes/medication use; PGS004889 includes a bundled clinical risk score), framework-origin with tiny incremental/PGS-only signal (PGS001272), or missing PRS-comparable metrics (e.g., PGS002757/PGS005113/PGS000728).

Its reported AUROC (0.78) is full-model and includes substantial clinical covariates, so it cannot be treated as PRS-only evidence; however, the per-SD OR (1.47) provides moderate standalone PRS signal support.

Top runners-up are drawn from the coherent five-biobank CKD benchmarking family (Am J Hum Genet, 2023-12-19) with consistent endpoint (“chronic kidney disease or dialysis”), no covariates reported (covariates=0), and large evaluation (n=90,274) across EUR+SAS—supportive for cleaner PRS signal interpretation and some ancestry breadth, but limited compared with PGS002237’s broader multi-ancestry evaluation. Within that family, PGS004158 (MultiPRS.CV) is preferred as an explicit multi-score aggregation (a positive structural signal for polygenic traits) and has the highest reported full-model AUROC/R² among siblings; PGS004030 (LDpred2-auto) is next best as a genome-wide shrinkage approach with very similar performance and large variant coverage. Confidence is Moderate because many candidates lack PRS-only metrics, several reported AUROCs are full-model and not directly comparable across differing covariate sets, and the strongest multi-ancestry candidate (PGS002237) still has covariate-heavy evaluation that limits direct inference about standalone PRS performance.

All 6 candidates are direct matches at the disease level (cirrhosis), but PRS-only metric cleanliness is uniformly weak: none report top-level PRS-comparable AUC/R2 (performance_metrics.auc/r2 and pgs_only_auc/pgs_only_r2 are all null), so full-model AUROC/C-index cannot be treated as standalone PRS performance. PGS004621 is preferred because it has exact trait alignment (trait_efo = cirrhosis of liver; phenotyping_reported = Cirrhosis), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with very large variant count (1,089,806), and comes from a disease-focused cirrhosis genetics study with broad multi-cohort context; its reported AUROC=0.68 is full-model and thus only weakly supportive, but covariates are basic (age/sex/PCs), reducing concern that the metric is heavily clinically inflated.

Runner-up PGS000726 also has exact trait_efo and phenotyping_reported = Cirrhosis, and provides PRS-relevant effect-size evidence (OR per SD 1.32; and OR top 20% vs bottom 20% 2.26), but it lacks any discrimination metric and is a sparse GW-significant score (12 variants), which is structurally less compelling for a polygenic endpoint.

Third, PGS000704 is endpoint-faithful for a major cirrhosis subtype (Alcoholic cirrhosis) and uses a multi-PRS snpnet approach with many variants (183,271), but it is subtype-restricted relative to the target (generic cirrhosis of liver) and only reports full-model C-index (0.711) plus a modest HR (1.18), offering limited clean PRS-only evidence.

Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL because the pool lacks PRS-only AUC/R2 across all candidates, forcing reliance on indirect/full-model metrics and structural proxies rather than clean standalone PRS performance.

All 6 candidates are direct matches to cirrhosis (some specifically alcohol-related). Under the requested focus on polygenic signal scale and transferability, PGS004621 is best supported because it is a genome-wide shrinkage PRS (PRS-CS) with very broad variant coverage (1,089,806 variants) and is developed/validated in a large multi-cohort, multi-biobank context (training cohorts listed: AllofUs, CHB, EB, FinnGen, IHCS, MyCode, UKB, deCODE) with a very large evaluation sample size (n=1,153,995) in EUR—features that most directly support robustness and external transportability. Across the pool, the absence of PRS-only AUC/R2 for essentially all candidates (and reliance on full-model AUROC/C-index) keeps the overall direct-match decision at sub-optimal quality rather than high-confidence.

All 6 candidates are direct matches to cholelithiasis (or a very close composite including cholecystitis). Under the requested focus on covariate cleanliness, packaging risk, and heritability-ceiling sanity checks, PGS001174 is the only model with explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC(no covariates)=0.62342; PGS R2(no covariates)=0.02808) plus incremental AUROC (0.04311) and a clearly basic covariate set (age, sex, array, PCs). Its PRS-only R2 is below the provided EUR h2_obs ceiling (0.0214) only in appearance because scales differ (observed-scale h2 vs reported R2), but it is not obviously implausible and does not exceed the liability-scale h2 (0.1372); importantly, the presence of PRS-only metrics allows a cleaner PRS-driven interpretation than competitors that report only partial-r or OR/beta. The main limitation is that PGS001174 comes from a known pan-trait UKB framework paper ("across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as often generalizing poorly; this prevents a high-quality designation despite clean covariates and good metric transparency.

Runners-up: PGS002072 and PGS001861 are from a portability framework (also UKB-based) and target a slightly broader endpoint (cholelithiasis + cholecystitis), but they at least report covariates that remain basic/demographic/PC-style and provide partial correlation with CIs (0.098 and 0.0948, respectively). Between them, PGS002072 is ranked above PGS001861 due to slightly stronger partial-r and a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with very large variant count, which is structurally favorable when performance metrics are otherwise sparse. Both remain limited by lack of PRS-only AUROC/R2 and by framework/portability study archetype.

The 2024 Commun Biol models (PGS004476/PGS004546) are penalized here because the paper context explicitly suggests risk-factor integration/metaPRS packaging and the covariates are listed as Unknown, making it hard to assess covariate cleanliness and PRS-driven contribution; they also provide only modest per-SD ORs (~1.22–1.30). PGS005150 is EAS-evaluated only with only a beta reported and minimal metric transparency, so it is less informative for general direct-match selection in this context.

All listed candidates are direct matches at the EFO level (chronic kidney disease), but most lack PRS-only performance metrics; under the requested PRS-metric cleanliness focus this materially limits confidence.

Runner-up 1 (PGS004158): Strong endpoint fidelity (CKD or dialysis) and a multi-score aggregation method (MultiPRS) is a positive structural signal. It also has the strongest reported discrimination among the five-biobank benchmarking family (full-model AUROC ~0.592; R2 ~0.020). However, these are not labeled PRS-only metrics (covariates reported as 0, but the metric type remains full-model in the record), so PRS-only cleanliness is unresolved.

Runner-up 2 (PGS002237): Very strong endpoint fidelity (CKD stage 3+; eGFR <45) and disease-focused publication (“Genome-wide polygenic score to predict chronic kidney disease across ancestries.”). But the only reported AUROC appears to be full-model (0.78) with a heavy clinical covariate set, and no PRS-only AUROC/R2 is provided—so the high AUROC is not interpretable as PRS performance under the cleanliness criterion.

Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL because direct-match candidates exist, but PRS-only metric reporting is largely absent and the only PRS-only-metric candidate is from a pan-trait framework with weak PRS-only discrimination and a less canonical CKD endpoint.

Main limitation lowering confidence: the evidence shown is dominated by full-model metrics (and many other candidates lack PRS-only metrics), and several other large-variant, large-sample breast cancer PRS exist in the list (e.g., PGS002242 with ~6.5M variants and very large evaluation n=343,676) but without comparable AUC/R² in the provided metadata, preventing a clean apples-to-apples transferability comparison beyond the well-characterized 2023 benchmarking cluster.

All three candidates are direct matches to Crohn disease by trait_efo and trait_reported/phenotyping_reported, but they differ in endpoint fidelity and PRS-only metric cleanliness. PGS000013 is best supported because it has strong endpoint fidelity (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both “Coronary artery disease”, trait_efo matches) and uniquely provides an explicit PRS-comparable metric (pgs_only_r2=0.04; also r2=0.04), avoiding reliance on covariate-inflated full-model AUROC.
