Under the covariate-cleanliness and PRS-driven-evidence focus, PGS000471 is best supported because within this otherwise near-clone set it shows the strongest available PRS-linked signals in the selected validation record: highest full-model AUROC (0.569) and strongest effect sizes (OR per SD 1.401; top 1% vs rest OR 3.77). PGS000470 is the next best-supported runner-up with intermediate full-model AUROC (0.557) and effect sizes (OR per SD 1.308; top 1% OR 2.45). PGS000469 ranks third despite a more polygenic method/variant count (PRS-CS; 1,119,238 variants) because its observed discrimination/effect sizes are weakest in the visible record (full-model AUROC 0.524; OR per SD 1.09; top 1% OR 1.48 with wide CI), and without PRS-only metrics we cannot verify that the larger genome-wide model is actually contributing more PRS signal.

Heritability-ceiling alignment cannot be cleanly assessed here because the candidates do not provide PRS-only R2; the reported full-model Nagelkerke R2 values are small and do not obviously violate the provided heritability ceiling guidance, but they are not directly comparable to h2_liability.

All four candidates are direct lexical matches to sarcoidosis, but the pool is dominated by UK Biobank framework/portability papers rather than a disease-focused multi-cohort sarcoidosis PRS, which lowers confidence in external robustness. Under the covariate-cleanliness focus, PGS000922 is reasonably clean (age/sex/array/PCs only) and, importantly, reports explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.64282; PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.01741), making it easier to interpret as PRS-driven rather than covariate-driven; its full-model AUROC (0.6486) is only slightly higher, consistent with limited covariate inflation. Its PRS-only R2 is also well below the provided liability-scale heritability ceiling (h2_liability=0.1070), so there is no heritability-ceiling conflict. Main limitation: it comes from the 'Significant sparse polygenic risk scores across 813 traits in UK Biobank' pan-trait sparse framework (snpnet) with very low variant count (12), a known warning context for generalization.

Runner-up PGS000923 is extremely similar (same framework paper and covariates) with slightly higher PRS-only AUROC (0.64561) and R2 (0.018) but uses a time-to-event endpoint ('TTE sarcoidosis'), which is a mild endpoint/packaging mismatch for generic disease risk and keeps it behind PGS000922 despite marginally better metrics. For the second runner-up, PGS002084 (LDpred2, 403,417 variants) has stronger methodological/packaging structure for polygenic signal capture than sparse models, but its performance reporting is weaker here (no PRS-only AUROC/R2; only partial correlation 0.0184 with covariates including deprivation index and birth date), and its trait_efo is 'skin sarcoidosis', introducing endpoint specificity ambiguity versus general sarcoidosis. PGS001872 is similar to PGS002084 but with fewer variants (79) and slightly higher partial-r (0.0199), leaving the two portability-paper models hard to separate; I favored PGS002084 for genome-wide shrinkage/coverage despite missing PRS-only discrimination metrics.

All five candidates include direct schizophrenia concept alignment via trait_reported/trait_efo, but only four (PGS000133/134/135/136) also have phenotype alignment (phenotyping_reported = "Schizophrenia"). PGS002785 is endpoint-mismatched (phenotyping_reported = "Cognitive function (Cognitive total)") and is therefore not a strong direct-match schizophrenia PRS despite the schizophrenia label.

Under the covariate-cleanliness focus, the PGS000133/134/135/136 cluster is relatively clean: all report only basic demographic/ancestry/batch covariates (age, sex, PCs, platform/batch), with no family-history bundling, biomarker/treatment adjustment, or risk-wrapper packaging visible. However, their reported discrimination is only full-model AUROC (no PGS-only AUROC/R2 and no incremental AUROC), which the domain guidance flags as non-substitutable for PRS-only performance; this materially limits confidence and also prevents a meaningful heritability-ceiling sanity check (the provided h2_liability is very low, but we lack PRS-only R2 to compare).

Within the clean schizophrenia-endpoint cluster, PGS000136 is preferred because it combines clean covariates with supportive PRS-driven evidence via a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.7, which the domain guidance treats as strong) and a modest full-model AUROC (0.64). PGS000133 is a close runner-up with similarly clean covariates and a strong OR (1.691) but lower full-model AUROC (0.60). PGS000135 has the highest full-model AUROC (0.74) but lacks effect-size reporting and is based on a much smaller validation sample (n=9,569), making it harder to judge whether the AUROC reflects PRS signal versus idiosyncrasies of that single evaluation; it remains a plausible alternative but not clearly best-supported given the missing PRS-only metrics.

All three candidates are direct matches to the target trait with consistent endpoint fields (trait_efo = skin carcinoma in situ; trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both “Carcinoma in situ of skin”), and all are evaluated in EUR with the same basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4) and the same validation sample size (n=5,500), so endpoint fidelity does not differentiate them. Under the PRS-only metric cleanliness focus, none reports PRS-only AUROC/R2 (pgs_only_auc/pgs_only_r2 are null for all), so the available AUROC/R2 are full-model and cannot be treated as comparable PRS-only performance; this makes the overall direct-match evidence sub-optimal. Given that limitation, PGS000471 is the best-supported within this sibling set because it shows the strongest available within-record signals (highest full-model AUROC 0.569 and highest reported per-SD effect size OR 1.401 with CI 1.297–1.513, plus strongest top-1% vs rest OR 3.77), while keeping the same clean/basic covariate set as the others. PGS000470 is the next-best runner-up (intermediate full-model AUROC 0.557 and OR 1.308), and PGS000469 ranks third despite a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS, 1,119,238 variants) because its observed effect sizes and full-model AUROC are materially weaker (AUROC 0.524; OR 1.09 with CI barely above 1), and without PRS-only metrics the method/variant-count advantage cannot be confirmed as translating into stronger standalone PRS performance.

Direct-match Hodgkin lymphoma candidates are present (PGS000637/PGS000638/PGS000639/PGS000640 all map to Hodgkin’s disease / Hodgkins lymphoma with matching phenotyping_reported). Under the requested focus on polygenic signal scale and transferability, PGS000639 is best supported within this direct-match set because it shows the strongest available validation signal among the Hodgkin-specific siblings (highest reported full-model AUROC=0.62 and highest reported Nagelkerke pseudo-R²=0.0276) while using basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4) and a modest but plausible variant set (20) consistent with a potentially less-diffuse architecture. Runners-up: PGS000638 has slightly weaker but still supportive performance (AUROC=0.601; pseudo-R²=0.0193) with similar endpoint/covariates; PGS000637 has much broader variant coverage (~1.05M) via PRS-CS (a structural plus for polygenic signal capture) but weaker reported performance here (AUROC=0.574; pseudo-R²=0.013) and the same EUR-only training/evaluation context.

Main limitation lowering confidence: all Hodgkin-specific models shown are trained and evaluated only in European ancestry with small reported training sample size (n=736) and modest validation size (n=775), and none reports clearly PRS-only discrimination metrics; additionally, another direct-match model (PGS003449) exists but has endpoint incoherence in the metadata (phenotyping_reported listed as chronic lymphocytic leukemia) and lacks comparable performance metrics, so it cannot be cleanly used to strengthen transferability evidence.

Direct-match candidates are present (sleep apnea / obstructive sleep apnea). Under the requested focus on polygenic signal scale and transferability, PGS005219 is best supported because it is a large-variant, genome-wide shrinkage/aggregation-style score (982,740 variants; weighted PRSsummation PRS-CSs) with explicit multi-cohort development (FinnGen, MGBB, MVP) and multi-ancestry evaluation noted (European, African American/Afro-Caribbean, East Asian, Hispanic/Latin American), which is the strongest visible transportability signal in this set. It also reports a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.98), supporting meaningful PRS signal magnitude.

Main limitation: the reported discrimination is only a full-model AUROC (0.79) with BMI included as a covariate, and no PGS-only AUROC/R2 is provided; per the domain guidance, full-model AUROC cannot be treated as PRS-comparable and may be covariate-influenced. Additionally, the endpoint is obstructive sleep apnea (BMI-adjusted), which is a clinically dominant subtype of sleep apnea (acceptable direct match) but still not identical to the generic label.

Runners-up: PGS005220 is nearly identical in design (984,184 variants; same study family, cohorts, and multi-ancestry evaluation) but has a weaker reported effect size (OR=1.53), so it ranks second. Among the remaining candidates, PGS003213 (PRS-CS; 1,111,194 variants) has the strongest polygenic-scale signal within the ExPRSweb framework cluster (highest full-model AUROC among those, 0.527, and strongest OR=1.106) and broad variant coverage, but it is EUR-only in GWAS/DEV/EVAL and comes from a pan-trait/framework-style repository (ExPRSweb), which lowers expected external transferability relative to the multi-cohort OSA scores.

Direct-match candidates are present for the target trait (sleep apnea), including multiple generic “Sleep apnea” models (PGS003204–PGS003218) and multiple “Obstructive sleep apnea” models (PGS003479, PGS003857, PGS003858, PGS005219, PGS005220). Endpoint fidelity is acceptable across these, and domain knowledge notes obstructive sleep apnea is the dominant clinical form of sleep apnea, so OSA-labeled models are valid direct matches.

However, PRS-only metric cleanliness is poor across the entire set: none of the candidates report PGS-only AUROC/R2 (pgs_only_auc and pgs_only_r2 are null throughout), so full-model AUROC cannot be treated as a comparable PRS metric. Under the stated perspective focus, this forces reliance on secondary signals (effect sizes, covariate burden, and study archetype).

PGS005220 is preferred because it is an OSA direct match with a strong reported PRS effect size (OR=1.53) and comes from a disease-focused OSA PRS publication (not the ExPRSweb framework family). Its reported AUROC (0.79) is full-model and includes BMI among covariates, so it is not clean PRS-only evidence, but the OR provides some PRS-specific support.

Runner-up PGS005219 is extremely similar (same publication family, same endpoint, same full-model AUROC and covariate set) and has an even stronger OR (1.98), but its label indicates BMI-adjusted/AdjustedBMI framing, which is a slightly less direct match to generic “sleep apnea” risk than the unadjusted-BMI variant given the endpoint-fidelity emphasis.

Third, PGS003213 is the strongest among the exact “Sleep apnea” (EFO sleep apnea) ExPRSweb cluster by full-model AUROC (0.527) and OR (1.106) with only basic demographic/PC covariates; but it is from a pan-trait/framework repository (ExPRSweb), which domain knowledge flags as typically underperforming disease-focused alternatives when endpoint-fidelity is otherwise acceptable.

Overall confidence is moderate (not high) because the pool lacks PRS-only performance metrics entirely, and several high full-model AUROCs are likely covariate-influenced (notably those including BMI), limiting clean PRS-only comparability.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (squamous cell carcinoma) are present (e.g., PGS000120, PGS000460–PGS000468, PGS000731, PGS005209). Endpoint fidelity is strongest for the Cancer PRSweb SCC models where trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all align to “Squamous cell carcinoma” and covariates are basic (age/sex/batch/PCs), avoiding explicit clinical/treatment packaging.

Under the PRS-only metric cleanliness focus, none of the direct SCC candidates report PGS-only AUROC or PGS-only R² (all pgs_only_* fields are null), so full-model AUROC cannot be treated as a clean PRS-comparable discriminator; this forces reliance on within-family consistency plus PRS-proxy signals (per-SD OR) and method/structure.

PGS000461 is selected because within the coherent SCC PRSweb cluster it shows the strongest per-SD effect size evidence (OR=1.491, 95% CI 1.395–1.593) alongside one of the higher reported AUROCs (full-model AUROC=0.599) with only basic covariates, and it is endpoint-faithful. The two runners-up (PGS000463 and PGS000465) are also endpoint-faithful PRSweb SCC models with similarly strong per-SD ORs (1.448 and 1.457, respectively) and comparable full-model AUROCs, but have slightly weaker effect-size support than PGS000461 in the visible metadata.

Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL (not high-quality) because the key PRS-only performance fields (PGS-only AUROC/R²) are missing across the candidate set, making it impossible to cleanly compare standalone PRS discrimination and increasing uncertainty about how much of the reported AUROC is covariate-driven.

Direct-match candidates for squamous cell carcinoma are present (e.g., PGS000120, PGS000460–PGS000468, PGS000731, PGS005209). Under the requested focus on polygenic signal scale and transferability, PGS000462 is best supported among the visible SCC models because it is endpoint-aligned (trait/phenotype both squamous cell carcinoma), has substantially larger training and validation samples than the MGI-based siblings (DEV n=61,038; EVAL n=60,018; EUR throughout), and shows non-trivial PRS signal via effect size (OR per SD 1.324) and full-model AUROC (0.573) with basic covariates (age/sex/batch/PCs). The top runners-up are PGS000464 (same UKB-based development size and endpoint; very similar performance with slightly higher full-model AUROC 0.575 and OR 1.332) and PGS000461 (MGI-based but shows stronger apparent discrimination/effect size—full-model AUROC 0.599 and OR 1.491—though with much smaller training/validation, which weakens transferability robustness under this perspective). Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL because all leading SCC candidates are EUR-only (limited ancestry transferability evidence) and the reported AUROCs are full-model (no explicit PRS-only AUROC/R²), making cross-model PRS signal comparisons less reliable.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (squamous cell carcinoma) are present (e.g., PGS000120, PGS000460–PGS000468, PGS000731, PGS005209). Under the covariate-cleanliness and PRS-driven-evidence focus, PGS000461 is preferred because it targets the exact endpoint (phenotyping_reported: squamous cell carcinoma) and uses only basic demographic/genetic-adjustment covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4), avoiding explicit clinical-risk packaging, family-history bundling, biomarker/treatment adjustment, or horizon-conditioned risk wrappers. It also shows comparatively strong PRS signal via effect size (OR per SD 1.491) and an extreme-tail contrast (top 1% vs rest OR 3.51), which is more indicative of PRS contribution than small differences in full-model AUROC among similarly adjusted models.

Top alternatives are PGS000463 and PGS000465: both are the same direct SCC endpoint with similarly clean covariates, and both show strong tail-risk ORs (3.74 and 4.54 respectively) with moderate-to-strong per-SD ORs (1.448 and 1.457). They rank behind PGS000461 mainly because the visible evidence does not include PRS-only AUROC/R2 for any of these, and their full-model AUROCs are not clearly superior in a way that can be attributed to PRS rather than covariates.

Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL (not DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY) because across the direct-match set, PRS-only performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R2 or incremental AUROC) are absent, so full-model AUROC cannot be treated as PRS-comparable; this limits confidence and makes it hard to assess alignment with the provided heritability ceiling (h2_liability=0.2317) beyond noting that the reported full-model metrics are modest and not obviously heritability-violating. Additionally, some direct-match options have problematic packaging/covariates (e.g., PGS005209 includes radiation/chemotherapy exposure and survivor-specific endpoint; PGS000731 has covariates listed as Unknown), reinforcing reliance on the cleaner PRSweb/Cancer PRSweb SCC models despite incomplete PRS-only metric reporting.

All listed candidates are direct matches to thyroid carcinoma/thyroid cancer by trait_efo, but they vary substantially in polygenic signal scale and transferability evidence. PGS005259 is preferred under the requested focus because it is a genome-wide PRS-CS–family score (~1.09M variants), developed in a large multi-biobank, explicitly multi-ancestry study context (many contributing cohorts listed) and evaluated in a multi-ancestry setting (MAE 100%), which is supportive for portability beyond a single-ancestry evaluation. It also reports a reasonably consistent full-model AUROC (~0.695) alongside a strong per-SD effect size (OR ~2.04), suggesting meaningful discriminative signal.

Key limitation: for PGS005259 (and the other 2026 medRxiv models), the GWAS ancestry is marked as NR and covariates are Unknown, and the reported AUROC appears to be full-model rather than PRS-only; this reduces comparability and makes it hard to separate PRS signal from covariate/modeling choices. Additionally, several older EUR-only models show higher full-model AUROC (e.g., PGS000208) but are based on very small SNP sets and EUR-only evaluation, offering weaker transferability evidence. Among runners-up, PGS001794 is also a genome-wide PRS-CS-auto score (~0.91M variants) from a large multi-biobank framework with very large EUR evaluation (n~358k), supporting stable estimation, while PGS005260 is a near-sibling genome-wide PRSCS model with similar MAE evaluation and effect size support but slightly weaker reported AUROC/effect size than PGS005259 in the provided metadata.

All listed candidates are direct matches at the concept level (trait_efo = type 1 diabetes mellitus), but many lack PRS-only performance reporting (pgs_only_auc/pgs_only_r2 are null) and instead report only full-model AUROC/C-index, which is not a valid substitute for PRS-only discrimination under the provided guidance. PGS001297 is best supported because it has high endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: Type 1 diabetes; trait_reported: Type 1 diabetes) and uniquely provides clean PRS-comparable metrics (pgs_only_auc=0.77118; pgs_only_r2=0.0912) alongside full-model metrics, enabling a PRS-only assessment without relying on covariate-boosted AUROC. The main limitation is that it comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper ("across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as often less externally robust than disease-focused scores, so despite clean PRS-only metrics the overall direct-match recommendation remains sub-optimal rather than high-confidence.

Runner-up PGS001296 is also from the same framework but still provides explicit PRS-only metrics (pgs_only_auc=0.68941; pgs_only_r2=0.05496) with a closely aligned endpoint (insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus time-to-event); it is penalized for time-to-event endpoint framing versus generic disease status and weaker PRS-only performance than PGS001297. Runner-up PGS004078 has strong endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: T1D; covariates: 0) and strong full-model AUROC/R2 (0.758/0.124), but it lacks explicit PRS-only metrics, so its apparent performance cannot be cleanly attributed to the PRS alone; it is therefore ranked behind the two snpnet models that report PRS-only AUC/R2.

Direct-match candidates are present for sleep apnea, including multiple exact-label “Sleep apnea” models (PGS003204–PGS003218) and clinically dominant-subtype “Obstructive sleep apnea” models (PGS003479, PGS003857/PGS003858, PGS005219/PGS005220), which domain knowledge treats as acceptable direct matches for a sleep-apnea target. Under the covariate-cleanliness and PRS-driven-evidence focus, the ExPRSweb sleep-apnea cluster has relatively clean/basic covariates (age/sex/batch/PCs/array) and avoids explicit clinical-risk packaging, family history, or biomarker-heavy adjustment; within that cluster, PGS003213 (PRS-CS; UKB development; full-model AUROC 0.527 with basic covariates) is the strongest-supported pick because it has the best discrimination among the clean-covariate, same-endpoint siblings and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) consistent with better polygenic signal capture than P+T/PLINK siblings. The main limitation is that none of the candidates report PRS-only AUROC/R2 or incremental AUROC, so the available AUROC values are full-model and cannot be confidently attributed to the PRS (and the trait’s low reported heritability ceiling further cautions against over-interpreting small AUROC differences). The OSA-labeled models with very high AUROC (e.g., PGS003857/PGS003858; PGS005219/PGS005220) are down-weighted here because their covariates explicitly include BMI (a strong mediator/clinical covariate for OSA) and they still lack PRS-only metrics, making the high AUROC likely covariate-driven and not clean evidence of standalone PRS performance. Runners-up are PGS003210 and PGS003211 because they share the same clean covariate set and endpoint family as PGS003213 and have the next-best full-model AUROC within that coherent cluster.

All shortlisted candidates are direct matches on concept (trait_efo = thyroid carcinoma; phenotyping_reported = thyroid cancer), but most records only report full-model AUROC (often with covariates), which is not PRS-comparable and is explicitly discounted under the provided domain guidance. Under the PRS-only metric cleanliness focus, PGS001289 is best supported because it reports explicit PRS-only metrics (pgs_only_auc = 0.61843 and pgs_only_r2 = 0.01236) alongside full-model metrics, enabling a clean standalone PRS assessment; its endpoint is a direct thyroid cancer phenotype. The main limitation is that it comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which the domain document flags as tending to generalize poorly, so the recommendation cannot be high-confidence.

The two strongest runners-up are PGS001794 and PGS001799 because they provide PRS-comparable R2 values (pgs_only_r2 reported as Nagelkerke’s R2 with covariates regressed out: 0.013659 and 0.010362, respectively) with direct thyroid cancer endpoints. They remain runners-up because PRS-only AUROC is not reported (only full-model AUROC is shown) and they originate from a broad framework-style global biobank analysis rather than a clearly thyroid-cancer–focused development/evaluation package. Many other direct-match candidates (e.g., PGS000208, PGS001354) show higher full-model AUROC, but lack PRS-only metrics and/or involve endpoint packaging/restriction (e.g., childhood cancer survivor subsequent thyroid cancer), making them less suitable under the PRS-only cleanliness and endpoint-fidelity emphasis.

All listed candidates are direct matches to thyroid carcinoma via trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, so the decision hinges on covariate cleanliness and whether reported performance is plausibly PRS-driven (since no trait-specific heritability ceiling is available in the provided domain_knowledge).

PGS001289 is best-supported under the covariate/packaging focus because it reports explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC (no covariates)=0.61843; PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.01236) alongside a modestly higher full-model AUROC (0.63744) with only basic demographic/PC/array covariates. This makes the performance evidence more clearly attributable to the PRS rather than covariate-driven uplift, and avoids red-flag clinical packaging (no family history, treatment, biomarkers, or horizon-conditioned risk wrapper).

Top alternatives: (1) PGS000209 has very clean covariates (gender, birth year only) and a large European evaluation sample (n=408,479), but it reports only full-model AUROC (0.694) with no PRS-only/incremental metric, so the PRS contribution cannot be isolated. (2) PGS001794 provides a PRS-comparable metric (Nagelkerke’s R2 with covariates regressed out=0.013659) and uses only demographic/PC-style covariates, but it is from a broad global-biobank framework context and still lacks an explicit PRS-only AUROC, leaving comparability less direct than PGS001289.

Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL because many candidates report only full-model AUROC (often with differing covariate sets, including family history in PGS000207/PGS000208/PGS000797 and treatment/survivor packaging in PGS001354/PGS005210), and no heritability ceiling is available here to sanity-check PRS-only R2/AUC magnitudes.

All 5 candidates are direct matches to ulcerative colitis by trait_efo, and most also by phenotyping_reported. Under the PRS-only metric cleanliness focus, PGS001306 is best supported because it reports explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.63006; PGS-only R2=0.02036) with basic covariates, and its PRS-only and full-model metrics are internally consistent on the same record (full-model AUROC=0.66162; incremental AUROC reported). PGS001307 is the closest runner-up with similarly clean PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.63847; PGS-only R2=0.02383), but its endpoint is time-to-event (phenotyping_reported: TTE ulcerative colitis), which is a mild endpoint-fidelity penalty versus a generic disease-status target. PGS004253 is ranked next because it has exact endpoint wording (phenotyping_reported: Ulcerative colitis) and a disease-focused publication context, but it lacks PRS-only AUROC/R2 (only full-model AUROC=0.66 and an OR are shown), so its discrimination evidence is less comparable under the stated perspective. Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL (not high quality) because several candidates lack PRS-only metrics (PGS001855/PGS002066/PGS004253), and the top two candidates with clean PRS-only metrics come from a pan-trait UKB framework paper, which introduces unresolved generalizability concerns despite clean reporting.

Direct-match candidates are present (all map to type 1 diabetes mellitus), but the pool shows heterogeneous study archetypes and many records lack PRS-only metrics, making a single clearly dominant choice hard.

Best pick (PGS002025): Among the visible direct matches, it has strong polygenic-signal scale (106,800 variants; genome-wide shrinkage via LDpred2) and is explicitly evaluated across multiple ancestry groups (AFR/EAS/EUR/GME/SAS), supporting transferability beyond EUR-only settings. It also has a large development sample (n=391,124) within the same portability study context, which—while a framework-style paper—still provides structured multi-ancestry evaluation metadata.

Top alternatives: (1) PGS001817 is from the same portability study with the same multi-ancestry evaluation breadth and large development sample, but uses far fewer variants (825), implying less polygenic coverage and potentially weaker capture of distributed signal. (2) PGS004162 reports strong full-model performance (AUROC ~0.77; R² ~0.14) and is explicitly a MultiPRS ensemble (a positive structural signal), but its training sample is very small (n=804) and evaluation is limited to EUR/SAS, which weakens transferability evidence relative to PGS002025.

Main limitation: Several disease-focused T1D scores (e.g., PGS000024) have very large validation samples but lack PRS-only metrics and have unclear covariate comparability; conversely, the portability-study models provide better multi-ancestry evaluation structure but are penalized by the framework archetype. This unresolved tradeoff keeps confidence below High.

Direct-match candidates for type 1 diabetes mellitus are present (multiple models with trait_efo=type 1 diabetes mellitus). Under the covariate-cleanliness focus, the strongest evidence cluster is the 2023 Am J Hum Genet “five biobanks” family where covariates are explicitly "0" (no non-genetic covariates), making the reported discrimination more plausibly PRS-driven than models reporting only full-model AUROC with clinical covariates or unknown covariates. Within that clean-covariate cluster, PGS004162 (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV) is preferred because it uses an explicit multi-score aggregation method (a positive structural signal) and reports strong full-model AUROC (~0.77) and R² (~0.14) without covariates, suggesting the metric is largely PRS-driven rather than covariate-driven. Heritability-ceiling alignment cannot be cleanly verified here because the reported R² scale (and whether it is directly comparable to liability h2_liability=0.2191) is not specified; however, it does not obviously exceed the ceiling and is more interpretable than covariate-inflated AUROCs (e.g., PGS000021 full-model AUROC 0.96 with autoantibodies/BMI/age). Top runners-up: PGS001297 is a direct T1D model with explicit PGS-only AUROC/R² and only basic demographic/PC/array covariates (clean packaging), but it comes from a pan-trait UKB framework paper (penalized sparse scores across 813 traits), which is a generalization-risk negative signal versus disease-focused benchmarking. PGS004078 is from the same clean-covariate five-biobanks family with similar endpoint and strong AUROC/R², but lacks the multi-score aggregation advantage that supports PGS004162. Remaining limitation: many other direct-match candidates have unknown covariates and/or only full-model AUROC, making cross-candidate performance comparability weak; thus confidence is moderate rather than high.

All 5 candidates are direct matches to ulcerative colitis by trait_efo, and most have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (UC diagnosis), except PGS001307 which is explicitly time-to-event (a mild endpoint mismatch for generic disease risk). Under the requested focus on covariate cleanliness and PRS-driven evidence, PGS001306 is best supported because it reports explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates = 0.63006; PGS R2 no covariates = 0.02036) alongside a basic covariate set (age, sex, array, PCs), allowing clearer separation of PRS signal from covariate-driven discrimination. Its PRS-only R2 is also comfortably below the provided liability-scale heritability ceiling (h2_liability=0.2646), which is directionally consistent with the sanity-check guidance.
